etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English assisten, from Old French assister (“to assist, to attend”), from Latin assistō (“stand at, bestand”, verb).

quote.citation: 2012 April 15, Phil McNulty, “Tottenham 1-5 Chelsea”, in BBC‎[1]:
quote.text: The referee seemed well placed to award the goal, but video evidence suggested the protests were well founded and the incident only strengthens the case of those lobbying for technology to assist officials.

definitions.definition: (sports) To make a pass that leads directly towards scoring.
(medicine) To help compensate for what is missing with the help of a medical technique or therapy.
(archaic) To stand (at a place) or to (an opinion).
(now archaic) To be present (at an event, occasion etc.).

quote.citation: 1789, Edward Gibbon, Memoirs of My Life, Penguin, published 1990, page 138:
quote.text: I assisted with pleasure at the representation of several tragedies and comedies.

quote.citation: 1967, The Rev. Loren Gavitt (ed.), Saint Augustine's Prayer Book: A Book of Devotion for members of the Episcopal Church, revised edition, West Park, NY: Holy Cross Publications, p. 8:
quote.text: To assist at Mass every Sunday and Holy Day of Obligation.

definitions.definition: A helpful action or an act of giving.
(soccer) A decisive pass made to the goal scorer

quote.citation: 2016 January 1, David Hytner, “Mesut Özil has Arsenal daring to dream of Premier League glory”, in The Guardian‎[2]:
quote.text: Özil has 16 assists in the Premier League and three goals; he has two more goals in the Champions League. On Monday, he took Bournemouth apart in the 2-0 win at the Emirates Stadium, setting up the first for Gabriel and scoring the second himself.

definitions.definition: (baseball) A defensive play, allowing a teammate to record a putout.
(sports) The act of helping another player score points or goals
